newsitem.title: USA: Harken Colombian well exceeds expectations.
newsitem.headline: Harken Colombian well exceeds expectations.

text.p: Harken Energy Corp said Thursday the Torcaz No. 2 produced at a rate of 635 barrels of oil daily on initial production tests, exceeding the company's expectations of 500 barrels per day.
The company said it will soon be applying to Ecopetrol, the Colombian state oil company, for an extended production and sales period.
Harken noted it has already identified eight additional well locations and has filed drilling permit applications with the Environmental Ministry for the next two wells.
Stating "We are now accelerating our plans to develop this field," Harken said it also plans to start four exploratory wells next year on other acreage in Colombia.
The Torcaz-2 well, located on Harken's Rio Negro Prospect in the Middle Magdalena Basin of Colombia, was drilled as planned to a total depth of 8,488 feet.
Drilling started in mid-July, about 6 weeks later than expected, and in mid-August the company said production results were expected by month end.

Harken said the "production testing phase was more complicated and time consuming than we originally expected due to unforseen difficulties with downhole pumps and higher than expected residual drilling fluid in the formation and well bore."
The company said it believes the well is currently producing primarily from the Mugrosa formation and that drilling mud and other solids remain in the lower potentially productive formations.
Accordingly, additional work will be undertaken in an attempt to remove any blocking debris throughout the entire section shown to be oil bearing on well log data.
"Clean-up" operations on the well will continue as it produces over the next few months with the goal of increasing production rates. -- New York Newsdesk 212-859-1610.
